correctness.rationale: For each \(k\ge2\), the first-one potential \(p=-\lambda\) has shift increment at most \(1\) for all binary de Bruijn edges; the sum on precisely the \(F_{k+2}\) required no-`11` edges is \(-(F_k-1)\). Every cyclic host therefore needs at least \(F_k-1\) extra factor occurrences, even if host factors `11` are allowed. Repeating once each edge \(0u0\) with legal nonzero \(u\) of length \(k-2\) adds exactly \(F_k-1\) edges, balances all vertices, and leaves a strongly connected legal graph; an Euler tour is an attaining cyclic host with no forbidden factors. The \(k=2\) boundary and Fibonacci counts were explicitly checked. Standalone finite verifier tests orders \(2\)–\(12\) and independently optimizes full-graph cases \(2\)–\(5\); finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison found Yu Hin Au’s treatment of primitive-word and power dictionaries (arXiv:0904.3997) and the classical shortest factor-witness framework in Tan–Shallit (arXiv:1304.3666v1) and the general circular min-cost-flow algorithm in Blanchet-Sadri–Lohr (DOI:10.1016/j.tcs.2015.06.038). None of these inspected texts states the exact Fibonacci–Lucas length for all no-11 binary target words, the unit-increment potential on the unrestricted host graph, or the exact \(0u0\) duplication pattern. The general algorithm computes finite instances but does not state this parametric symbolic optimum. Targeted aliases were searched; no directly covering statement was found, subject to residual literature risk.
residual_risks: General min-cost-flow tools can compute every fixed order; an unindexed separate symbolic evaluation may exist, including under constrained-coding terminology.

value.rationale: The golden-mean/no-adjacent-ones language is a natural constrained binary sequence family, not an arbitrary sliced example. The exact Lucas length and Fibonacci repetition overhead resolve a full infinite family of minimum circular factor-cover instances. The proof also establishes the non-obvious equality between unrestricted hosts and constraint-respecting hosts, with an explicit sparse duplication construction and a sharp dual witness. These are structurally meaningful beyond a routine count of legal words.
